# Finneas, Ace Archer: Rabbits, Tokens and Counters

- **Format:** Commander (100 cards)
- **Archetype:** Go-wide Rabbits and tokens. Every Finneas attack puts +1/+1 counters on your other tokens and Rabbits, anthems make the team bigger, and Overrun or a flying alpha strike finishes. Proactive creature midrange.
- **Played by:** either. Best for whoever enjoyed the Bloomburrow Rabbit starter deck and likes building a wide board. It is the natural third deck next to Giada and Gisa.
- **Status:** idea
- **Target bracket:** 2 (Core)
- **Complexity:** 3/5
- **Estimated power:** 5.5 with owned cards only, 6.5 with the buys
- **Configuration:** **Commander** set (builds alongside Giada and Gisa). It shares 24 cards with the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck and 6 with Gruul Ramp, so build one or the other, or buy the duplicates listed under Tier 2.

Finneas, Ace Archer is a cheap 2-mana Rabbit commander. Every time he attacks, each other Rabbit and each token you control gets a +1/+1 counter. The deck fills the board with Rabbits and little 1/1 tokens, turns them into a real army with those counters and anthems, then wins with one big attack: Overrun, or an Abzan Falconer turn where every creature with a counter flies. It suits whoever enjoyed the Bloomburrow Rabbit starter deck: lots of creatures, simple choices each turn and a satisfying finish. Because the commander costs only 2, it starts fast and is easy to recast.

### Why these buys (in priority order)

1. **1x Valley Questcaller** (replaces Crusader of Odric). A Rabbit lord. Every other Rabbit you control, including Rabbit tokens from Hop to It, Carrot Cake, Head of the Homestead and Cadira, gets +1/+1, and you scry 1 each time one or more other Rabbits enter. It is the biggest single upgrade. *Also useful in: the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck (its target list plays 3, so buy 4 in total if both decks are kept).*
2. **1x Intangible Virtue** (replaces Resolute Reinforcements). All your creature tokens get +1/+1 and vigilance. Tokens can then attack and still block, and they survive Sunblast Angel, which destroys tapped creatures. *Also useful in: any white tokens deck (not in the current Selesnya Rabbits lists).*
3. **1x Harvestrite Host** (replaces Helpful Hunter). A 3/3 Rabbit. Whenever it or another Rabbit enters, a creature gets +1/+0, and the second time that happens in a turn you draw a card (at most one card per turn). Hop to It, Head of the Homestead and Cadira each set that off on their own, so it draws a card most turns you add Rabbits, instead of Helpful Hunter's single card. *Also useful in: the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck (its target list plays 2, so buy 3 in total if both decks are kept).*
4. **1x Abzan Falconer** (replaces Syr Alin, the Lion's Claw). Each creature you control with a +1/+1 counter has flying. Finneas's counters land before blockers are chosen, so everything that just got a counter flies in that same attack. It is a cheap, telegraphed win condition that suits Bracket 2. *Also useful in: any future white counters deck.*
5. **1x Good-Fortune Unicorn** (replaces Wildwood Scourge). Whenever another creature you control enters, tokens included, it gets a +1/+1 counter. That feeds Byrke's doubling, Abzan Falconer's flying and Inspiring Call's draw. *Also useful in: any G/W counters deck (not in the current Selesnya Rabbits lists).*
6. **1x Inspiring Call** (replaces Adamant Will). An instant that draws a card for each creature you control with a +1/+1 counter (often 4–6 after a Finneas attack) and makes those creatures indestructible until end of turn. Cast in response to a destroy-all wipe such as Austere Command or Cleansing Nova, it saves every creature with a counter. Tokens without a counter still die, and it does nothing against -X/-X. *Also useful in: any green counters deck.*
7. **1x Pollen-Shield Hare // Hare Raising** (replaces Dawnwing Marshal). A second token anthem (+1/+1 to your creature tokens) on a 2/2 Rabbit body. The adventure half, Hare Raising, is a {G} sorcery: one creature gets +X/+X and vigilance, where X is the number of creatures you control. Cast it on Finneas before combat to make him safe to attack with, then cast the Hare later from exile. *Also useful in: could suit the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck (not in its current list).*
8. **1x Cadira, Caller of the Small** (replaces Cat Collector). A 3/3 trample for 3. When it deals combat damage to a player, it makes a 1/1 Rabbit for each token you control, which doubles a token board. *Also useful in: could suit the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck (not in its current list).*
9. **1x Head of the Homestead** (replaces Prideful Parent). Three Rabbits for 5 mana (a 3/2 plus two 1/1 Rabbit tokens). On its own it triggers Harvestrite Host three times, so it draws that turn's card. *Also useful in: could suit the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck (not in its current list).*
10. **1x Rampant Growth** (replaces Grow from the Ashes). 2-mana ramp instead of 3, so 4-drops come out on turn 3. *Also useful in: any green Commander deck.*
11. **1x Farseek** (replaces Druid of the Cowl). 2-mana ramp that survives board wipes. In this deck it fetches a Plains or a Canopy Vista (which has the Plains type), tapped. It also frees Druid of the Cowl for the Gruul 60-card deck. *Also useful in: any green Commander deck; frees a Gruul card.*
12. **1x Claim Jumper** (replaces Springbloom Druid). A 3/3 vigilance Rabbit. When it enters, if an opponent controls more lands than you, you may put a Plains card (a basic Plains or Canopy Vista) onto the battlefield tapped, then a second one if an opponent still has more. It is ramp on a real body, best when you're behind on lands. *Also useful in: could suit the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck (not in its current list).*
13. **1x Conclave Tribunal** (replaces Repel Calamity). Exiles any nonland permanent an opponent controls until Tribunal leaves. Convoke lets you tap creatures, tokens included, to pay for it, so it often costs 1–2 real mana. *Also useful in: Giada or any white deck.*
14. **1x Rootborn Defenses** (replaces Charming Prince). Instant-speed board-wipe protection: every creature you control gains indestructible until end of turn, and it populates (makes a copy of one of your creature tokens). It doesn't stop -X/-X. *Also useful in: —.*
15. **1x Path to Exile** (replaces Rabid Bite). 1-mana instant that exiles any creature (its controller may fetch a basic land). Unlike Rabid Bite, it doesn't need a big creature of yours and it beats indestructible. Reprinted in Reality Fracture Commander (2 Oct 2026); MTGMate already stocks it at reprint prices (A$4.00 on 2026-09-28), so there's no need to wait. *Also useful in: the Giada target list also wants one (buy 2).*
16. **1x Canopy Vista** (replaces Forest). A G/W dual that enters untapped once you control two basic lands. It has the Forest and Plains types, so Farseek and Claim Jumper can fetch it. *Also useful in: could suit the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck (its target list uses Sunpetal Grove).*
17. **1x Sunpetal Grove** (replaces Plains). A G/W checkland that enters untapped if you control a Forest or Plains, so it's usually untapped. It helps the GGG and WW costs. *Also useful in: the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck (its target list plays 2, so buy 3 in total if both decks are kept).*
18. **1x Fortified Village** (replaces Forest). A G/W dual that enters untapped if you reveal a Forest or Plains card from your hand. *Also useful in: could suit the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck (not in its current list).*

### Shared-pool conflicts

Each physical card can only be in one deck at a time. These decks need some of the same copies:

- [Mono-White Angels](../casual/mono-white-angels.md): 4 cards between the owned lists, 3 between the target lists. Inspiring Overseer, Stasis Snare, Swords to Plowshares, Valorous Stance.
- [Gruul Ramp](../casual/gruul-ramp.md): 6 cards between the owned lists, 5 between the target lists. Druid of the Cowl, Eternal Witness, Garruk's Uprising, Rampaging Baloths, Sakura-Tribe Elder, Scavenging Ooze.
- [Selesnya Rabbits](../casual/selesnya-rabbits.md): 24 cards between the owned lists, 16 between the target lists. Beast Within, Burrowguard Mentor, Byrke, Long Ear of the Law, Carrot Cake, Crusader of Odric, Dawnwing Marshal, Druid of the Spade, Felling Blow, Finneas, Ace Archer, Harmonize, Helpful Hunter, Hop to It, Mentor of the Meek, Overrun, Prideful Parent, Rabbit Response, Rabid Bite, Regal Caracal, Release the Dogs, Resolute Reinforcements, Selesnya Guildgate, Temple of Plenty, Warren Elder, Wilt-Leaf Liege.
- [Orzhov Vampires](../casual/orzhov-vampires.md): 1 cards between the owned lists, 1 between the target lists. Evolving Wilds.
- [Orzhov Removal Midrange](../casual/orzhov-removal.md): 5 cards between the owned lists, 4 between the target lists. Cathar Commando, Inspiring Overseer, Stasis Snare, Swords to Plowshares, Valorous Stance.

Shares no physical cards with: [Mono-Black Zombies](../casual/mono-black-zombies.md), [Izzet Prowess](../casual/izzet-prowess.md), [Mono-Black Midrange](../casual/mono-black-midrange.md), [Giada, Font of Hope: Calling All Angels (upgraded)](giada-angels.md), [Ghoulcaller Gisa: Wretched Ranks (upgraded)](gisa-zombies.md).

## Substitutes

The Owned-only version below is what you play until the buys arrive. Each target buy has an owned stand-in:

| Target buy | Owned stand-in until it arrives | What the stand-in costs the deck |
|---|---|---|
| Valley Questcaller | Crusader of Odric | **Large.** No Rabbit lord. Crusader is one big body, not a team boost |
| Intangible Virtue | Resolute Reinforcements | **Medium.** Tokens stay 1/1 and tap when attacking, so Sunblast Angel can punish them |
| Harvestrite Host | Helpful Hunter | **Medium.** One card once, instead of up to a card every turn you add two or more Rabbits |
| Abzan Falconer | Syr Alin, the Lion's Claw | **Medium.** No way to give the team flying; you rely on Overrun or trample to get through |
| Good-Fortune Unicorn | Wildwood Scourge | **Medium.** New tokens don't get a counter (only Serra Redeemer gives them one), so there are fewer counters for Byrke, Abzan Falconer and Inspiring Call |
| Inspiring Call | Adamant Will | **Medium.** Protects one creature instead of every creature with a counter, and draws nothing |
| Pollen-Shield Hare // Hare Raising | Dawnwing Marshal | **Small–medium.** Loses the second token anthem; Marshal's pump costs 5 mana |
| Cadira, Caller of the Small | Cat Collector | **Medium.** Loses the token-doubling threat; Cat Collector needs lifegain to make Cats |
| Head of the Homestead | Prideful Parent | **Small.** 2 bodies instead of 3, and no Rabbits |
| Rampant Growth | Grow from the Ashes | **Small.** Ramp one turn later |
| Farseek | Druid of the Cowl | **Tiny.** Similar speed; the dork dies to wipes. The swap mainly frees Druid for the Gruul deck |
| Claim Jumper | Springbloom Druid | **Small.** Similar ramp, but a 1/1 instead of a 3/3 Rabbit |
| Conclave Tribunal | Repel Calamity | **Small–medium.** Only kills creatures with power or toughness 4 or more; no answer to enchantments, artifacts or planeswalkers |
| Rootborn Defenses | Charming Prince | **Medium at the LGS.** The owned list has no spell that saves the whole team from a board wipe (Inspiring Call is a buy too) |
| Path to Exile | Rabid Bite | **Medium.** Sorcery speed, needs a big creature of yours, and it deals damage, so indestructible creatures survive it |
| Canopy Vista, Sunpetal Grove, Fortified Village | 2 Forest + 1 Plains | **Small.** Slightly worse colour mix in the first turns |

Overall the owned list is about 5.5 and the target list about 6.5. The first seven buys (Questcaller, Virtue, Host, Falconer, Unicorn, Inspiring Call, Pollen-Shield Hare) give most of the gain for about A$3 estimated (A$8.60 at MTGMate on 2026-09-28, though Abzan Falconer and Pollen-Shield Hare were out of stock that day).

## Notes

### Game plan (plain words)
These notes describe the target list. Until the buys arrive, the owned list uses the stand-ins in Substitutes.

Finneas is a small 2/2 Rabbit.
- **Tokens** are creatures made by a card. For example, Hop to It makes three 1/1 Rabbits. The deck fills the board with small creatures, both Rabbits and tokens.
- **Whenever Finneas attacks**, every *other* token and every other Rabbit you control gets a **+1/+1 counter**. A counter is a permanent marker: that creature stays 1 bigger for the rest of the game. Then, if your creatures add up to 10 or more power, you draw a card.
- **Anthems** are cards that make many creatures bigger at once: Wilt-Leaf Liege (your other green and white creatures), Intangible Virtue and Pollen-Shield Hare (your creature tokens), and Valley Questcaller (your other Rabbits).
- Over a few turns your 1/1s grow into 3/3s and 4/4s. Then one big attack wins: Overrun (+3/+3 and trample for everyone), Rabbit Response, Jazal Goldmane, Warren Elder's pump, or Abzan Falconer. Falconer gives flying to every creature with a +1/+1 counter. Finneas's counters land before blockers are chosen, so the creatures that just got one fly in that same attack.

Turn by turn:
1. **Turns 1–3:** play a land every turn. Play **ramp**, meaning cards that give you extra mana: Llanowar Elves, Sakura-Tribe Elder, Rampant Growth, Farseek, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet. Cast Finneas from the command zone on turn 2 or 3.
2. **Turns 3–6:** add token makers and Rabbits (Hop to It, Release the Dogs, Imperious Perfect, Regal Caracal, Head of the Homestead), one anthem, and card draw (Mentor of the Meek, Harvestrite Host, Harmonize).
3. **Attack with Finneas whenever it's safe.** He has **vigilance**, so attacking doesn't tap him and he can still block. He has **reach**, so he can block flyers.
4. **Finish** with a team pump when opponents are low on life or short of blockers.

### Opening hand and mulligan
- **Keep:** 3–4 lands, or 2 lands plus a ramp card (Llanowar Elves, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Rampant Growth, Farseek), and something to cast on turns 2–4. Finneas is always available in the command zone, so your hand doesn't need him.
- **Mulligan** (shuffle, draw a new 7, then put 1 card on the bottom for each mulligan you've taken): 0–1 lands, 6–7 lands, or 2 lands where everything costs 4 or more.
- In multiplayer your first mulligan is free (Comprehensive Rules 103.5c): draw a new 7 and keep all of them; after that each mulligan puts one card on the bottom.

### Play tips
1. **Pick who to attack.** In multiplayer you choose which opponent each creature attacks. Send Finneas at the player with no good untapped blockers. His trigger happens as soon as he is declared as an attacker, so your team already has its counters before blocks. He is only a 2/2, though. If something big might block him, keep Valorous Stance (indestructible) ready. Snakeskin Veil stops targeted removal, but in combat it only makes him a 3/3.
2. **Don't dump your whole hand.** **Board wipes** (cards that destroy every creature) are common at Commander nights. Once you have 5–6 creatures and an anthem, hold one or two token makers back. Leave 3 mana open when an opponent has 4+ mana and cards in hand: Rootborn Defenses protects every creature, Inspiring Call protects only creatures with a +1/+1 counter (and draws a card for each). Indestructible does nothing against -X/-X effects such as Massacre Wurm, Crippling Fear or Toxic Deluge.
3. **Vigilance protects you.** Intangible Virtue gives your tokens vigilance, so they don't tap when they attack. They can still block, and they survive Sunblast Angel, which only destroys *tapped* creatures.
4. **Count before Overrun.** Every creature gets +3/+3 and trample, so 8 creatures means 24 extra damage. It's a sorcery, so cast it before combat, after your creatures for the turn are down, and split attackers so each opponent can't block them all.
5. **Commander tax.** If Finneas dies, put him back in the command zone. Each recast costs {2} more (4, then 6…). He's cheap, so recast him. Late in the game, Warren Elder, Jazal Goldmane, Scavenging Ooze and Crawling Barrens soak up spare mana.

### Cards to watch out for from opponents
- **Giada (Angels):**
  - Austere Command and Cleansing Nova destroy creatures. They're sorceries, so they come on Giada's turn. Hold back, and answer with Rootborn Defenses (whole team) or Inspiring Call (creatures with counters).
  - Sunblast Angel destroys tapped creatures. Vigilance beats it.
  - Archangel of Tithes: while it's untapped, you pay {1} for each creature that attacks Giada's player. Attack someone else, or remove it with Swords, Path or Conclave Tribunal before your big turn.
  - Also watch for her big flyers. Finneas and Clifftop Lookout have reach and can block them.
- **Gisa (Zombies):**
  - Massacre Wurm gives your creatures -2/-2 and makes you lose 2 life for each one that dies. Anthems and counters are your defence, because a 3/3 survives it.
  - Crippling Fear (upgraded Gisa list) gives -3/-3 to every creature that isn't the chosen type (Gisa picks Zombie), which is nearly a full wipe for you. Keep a token maker in hand to rebuild.
  - Fleshbag Marauder makes each player sacrifice a creature. Sacrifice a token, never Finneas.
  - Grave Titan is a big threat that makes more Zombies. Save Swords, Path or Beast Within for it.
- **At the LGS:**
  - Wraths such as Wrath of God, Blasphemous Act and Toxic Deluge (-X/-X gets around indestructible).
  - Ghostly Prison and Propaganda make you pay per attacker.
  - Big flyers.
  - Against stronger opponents, expect Finneas to be removed. Don't rely on one creature, and recast him.
- **Table talk:** before the game, say "Bracket 2 Rabbit tokens deck, no Game Changers, no combos."

### Sharing cards with the 60-card decks
- **Selesnya Rabbits:** Finneas shares 24 owned cards with the 60-card Selesnya Rabbits deck (16 once both decks are on their target lists), so build one or the other, or buy the duplicates in Tier 2 section B.
- **Gruul Ramp:** Finneas also shares 6 cards with the 60-card Gruul Ramp deck: Druid of the Cowl, Eternal Witness, Garruk's Uprising, Rampaging Baloths, Sakura-Tribe Elder and Scavenging Ooze. Building Finneas takes Gruul Ramp apart unless you buy the duplicates in Tier 2 section C (the Farseek buy frees Druid of the Cowl).
- **Orzhov Vampires:** Finneas shares 1 card with it, Evolving Wilds. Buy a third copy or play a basic land in its place.
- The Shared-pool conflicts section above lists every overlap.

Finneas also shares 6 cards with the 60-card Gruul Ramp deck (Druid of the Cowl, Eternal Witness, Garruk's Uprising, Rampaging Baloths, Sakura-Tribe Elder, Scavenging Ooze) and 1 with Orzhov Vampires (Evolving Wilds).

Recomputed 2026-09-28 against the Gruul Ramp target list (A$ est): Eternal Witness 2.09, Garruk's Uprising 0.73, Rampaging Baloths 0.41, Sakura-Tribe Elder 0.47, Scavenging Ooze 0.27.
